# Overlay for installing examples/mcp-server.yaml on kind. It replaces the
# placeholders with the fixtures in ../fixtures/ and scales the example down
# to fit a hosted runner. No ingress controller runs, so the Ingress objects
# are created but serve nothing; https-ingress covers routing.
queueMode:
  workerReplicaCount: 1
webhookProcessor:
  replicaCount: 1
database:
  host: postgres
redis:
  host: redis

# n8n with PostgreSQL and Worker

Starts n8n with PostgreSQL as database, Redis for queue management, and a Worker as a separate container. Task runner sidecar containers are included for executing Code nodes (JavaScript/Python), as required by n8n 2.0+.

## Start

To start n8n simply start docker-compose by executing the following
command in the current folder.

**IMPORTANT:** But before you do that change the default users, passwords, and tokens in the [`.env`](.env) file!

```
docker compose up -d
```

To stop it execute:

```
docker compose stop
```

## Configuration

The default name of the database, user and password for PostgreSQL can be changed in the [`.env`](.env) file in the current directory.

The `RUNNERS_AUTH_TOKEN` in the [`.env`](.env) file is a shared secret used for authentication between n8n and the task runner containers. Generate a secure random value for production use.

## Upgrade Considerations

### PostgreSQL 18

This example runs `postgres:18`.

The compose file pins `PGDATA` to `/var/lib/postgresql/data`. Postgres 18 changed where it stores
data by default, and pinning it keeps the volume mount stable across major versions. Don't remove
that line, or the database will start empty on an existing volume.

### Installing fresh

Nothing to do. Run `docker compose up -d`.

### Upgrading an existing setup

This is a major version upgrade and it is breaking. Postgres 18 cannot read a data directory written
by 16, so bumping the image alone stops with:

```
FATAL:  database files are incompatible with server
```

Nothing is deleted, and you can pin the image back to `postgres:16` at any point.

Follow the official guide,
[Upgrading a PostgreSQL Cluster](https://www.postgresql.org/docs/18/upgrading.html). Pick a method
based on your database size and how much downtime you can take.

For a small setup, dump and restore is usually simplest. n8n is offline while you do it:

```bash
# 0. Load .env into your shell. Compose reads it, your shell does not
set -a && . ./.env && set +a

# 1. Export, with your old setup still running
docker compose exec -T postgres pg_dumpall -U "$POSTGRES_USER" > n8n-backup.sql

# 2. Check the export worked. This must print 1
grep -c "PostgreSQL database cluster dump complete" n8n-backup.sql

# 3. Stop, and delete ONLY the database volume. The guard repeats the check, so a
#    failed export stops here instead of falling through to the delete
grep -q "PostgreSQL database cluster dump complete" n8n-backup.sql \
  && docker compose down \
  && docker volume rm withpostgresandworker_db_storage

# 4. Start ONLY the database and import into it. Bringing the whole stack up here
#    lets n8n build its schema first, and the import then collides with it
docker compose up -d postgres
docker compose exec -T postgres psql -U "$POSTGRES_USER" -d "$POSTGRES_DB" < n8n-backup.sql

# 5. Import done, now start the rest
docker compose up -d
```

### Gotchas

Things the PostgreSQL guide will not tell you, because they are specific to this setup.

- **Never use `docker compose down -v` here.** That also deletes `n8n_storage`, which holds n8n's
  local state. Keep your `.env` too: this example sets `N8N_ENCRYPTION_KEY` from it, and without
  that key your saved credentials cannot be decrypted, even with the database restored. Delete only `withpostgresandworker_db_storage`.
- **`role "..." already exists` and `database "..." already exists` on import are expected.** The
  container creates both on first start. Your data still imports.
- **Staying on 16 is fine.** It is still supported. Pin the image back to `postgres:16`.

# n8n with PostgreSQL

Starts n8n with PostgreSQL as database.

## Start

To start n8n with PostgreSQL simply start docker-compose by executing the following
command in the current folder.

**IMPORTANT:** But before you do that change the default users and passwords in the [`.env`](.env) file!

```
docker compose up -d
```

To stop it execute:

```
docker compose stop
```

## Configuration

The default name of the database, user and password for PostgreSQL can be changed in the [`.env`](.env) file in the current directory.

## Upgrade Considerations

### PostgreSQL 18

This example runs `postgres:18`.

The compose file pins `PGDATA` to `/var/lib/postgresql/data`. Postgres 18 changed where it stores
data by default, and pinning it keeps the volume mount stable across major versions. Don't remove
that line, or the database will start empty on an existing volume.

### Installing fresh

Nothing to do. Run `docker compose up -d`.

### Upgrading an existing setup

This is a major version upgrade and it is breaking. Postgres 18 cannot read a data directory written
by 16, so bumping the image alone stops with:

```
FATAL:  database files are incompatible with server
```

Nothing is deleted, and you can pin the image back to `postgres:16` at any point.

Follow the official guide,
[Upgrading a PostgreSQL Cluster](https://www.postgresql.org/docs/18/upgrading.html). Pick a method
based on your database size and how much downtime you can take.

For a small setup, dump and restore is usually simplest. n8n is offline while you do it:

```bash
# 0. Load .env into your shell. Compose reads it, your shell does not
set -a && . ./.env && set +a

# 1. Export, with your old setup still running
docker compose exec -T postgres pg_dumpall -U "$POSTGRES_USER" > n8n-backup.sql

# 2. Check the export worked. This must print 1
grep -c "PostgreSQL database cluster dump complete" n8n-backup.sql

# 3. Stop, and delete ONLY the database volume. The guard repeats the check, so a
#    failed export stops here instead of falling through to the delete
grep -q "PostgreSQL database cluster dump complete" n8n-backup.sql \
  && docker compose down \
  && docker volume rm withpostgres_db_storage

# 4. Start ONLY the database and import into it. Bringing the whole stack up here
#    lets n8n build its schema first, and the import then collides with it
docker compose up -d postgres
docker compose exec -T postgres psql -U "$POSTGRES_USER" -d "$POSTGRES_DB" < n8n-backup.sql

# 5. Import done, now start the rest
docker compose up -d
```

### Gotchas

Things the PostgreSQL guide will not tell you, because they are specific to this setup.

- **Never use `docker compose down -v` here.** That also deletes `n8n_storage`, which holds your
  encryption key. You would restore the database fine and every saved credential would be unreadable. Delete only `withpostgres_db_storage`.
- **`role "..." already exists` and `database "..." already exists` on import are expected.** The
  container creates both on first start. Your data still imports.
- **Staying on 16 is fine.** It is still supported. Pin the image back to `postgres:16`.

# Throwaway Redis for the kind install test. Not a recommendation for running
# Redis in production.
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: redis
  labels:
    app: redis
spec:
  replicas: 1
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: redis
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: redis
    spec:
      containers:
        - name: redis
          image: redis:8.10.2-alpine
          ports:
            - containerPort: 6379
          readinessProbe:
            exec:
              command: ["redis-cli", "ping"]
            periodSeconds: 2
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: Service
metadata:
  name: redis
spec:
  selector:
    app: redis
  ports:
    - port: 6379
      targetPort: 6379

# Throwaway Postgres for the kind install test. Not a recommendation for
# running Postgres in production. The password comes from n8n-db-secret, the
# same Secret the chart reads, which the workflow creates first.
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: postgres
  labels:
    app: postgres
spec:
  replicas: 1
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: postgres
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: postgres
    spec:
      containers:
        - name: postgres
          image: postgres:18.4-alpine
          ports:
            - containerPort: 5432
          env:
            - name: POSTGRES_USER
              value: n8n
            - name: POSTGRES_DB
              value: n8n
            - name: POSTGRES_PASSWORD
              valueFrom:
                secretKeyRef:
                  name: n8n-db-secret
                  key: password
          readinessProbe:
            exec:
              command: ["pg_isready", "-U", "n8n", "-d", "n8n"]
            periodSeconds: 2
          volumeMounts:
            - name: data
              mountPath: /var/lib/postgresql
      volumes:
        - name: data
          emptyDir: {}
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: Service
metadata:
  name: postgres
spec:
  selector:
    app: postgres
  ports:
    - port: 5432
      targetPort: 5432

# 0007. Every example installs in CI, with the add-ons it expects

Date: 2026-09-25
PR: https://github.com/n8n-io/n8n-hosting/pull/215

## Context

Decision 0006 installed the three examples that need only Postgres and Redis. The rest expect things the chart does not deploy and a bare kind cluster does not have: KEDA, an ingress controller, a certificate issuer, S3, nodes in named pools, or an enterprise licence. The examples are the supported way to run the chart, so an example that CI only renders can stop installing without anyone noticing.

## Decision

Every example has an install leg. An example that expects something from the cluster gets it from a pre-install hook, `ci/install/<example>.pre.sh`. A post-install hook, `ci/install/<example>.post.sh`, checks that the example works with it. A leg that needs more than one node brings a kind config in `ci/kind/`. This follows the chart's list of what the core expects the cluster to provide in `DESIGN.md`: CI plays the cluster, and the chart still installs none of it.

Add-ons come from their own projects' Helm charts, pinned to a version: KEDA from `kedacore`, ingress-nginx, cert-manager from `jetstack`, and the Traefik and Prometheus Operator CRDs for `extra-objects`. These are the charts those projects publish and maintain, unlike the datastore charts decision 0006 moved away from. Datastores stay plain manifests, and S3 comes from Adobe S3Mock in `ci/fixtures/s3/`.

CI cannot reach Let's Encrypt, so the ingress leg runs a CA issuer under the name the example uses. The licensed legs read the enterprise test licence from repo secrets. Pull requests from forks do not receive those secrets, so the licensed legs are left out there.

## Consequences

- An install break in any example fails `install-test` on labelled, bump and release pull requests.
- The checks cover what the chart renders, not what the add-on does later. The KEDA leg proves the ScaledObject is accepted and its HPA reads the queue, not that workers scale out. Fuller behaviour belongs in n8n's end-to-end suite.
- Add-on and fixture versions are pinned in the hooks and fixtures, and move by hand.
- Overlays scale examples down to fit a hosted runner, and switch off what the fixtures cannot provide, such as Postgres TLS. Each overlay says what it changes and why.

# 0006. The install test runs examples on kind against plain Postgres and Redis

Date: 2026-09-24
PR: https://github.com/n8n-io/n8n-hosting/pull/211

## Context

The chart's install test installed the chart defaults, not an example. It took Postgres and Redis from the Bitnami chart repository. Bitnami moved its versioned images to `bitnamilegacy` in August 2025 and is expected to withdraw the chart repository too. A test that depends on that repository would then stop running.

The Helm E2E suite in `n8n-io/n8n` also installs this chart. It installs the chart from `main` on k3s with `examples/minimal.yaml` or `examples/standalone.yaml`, then runs part of n8n's Playwright suite.

## Decision

Fuller end-to-end tests against an n8n build belong in n8n's own test suite or elsewhere. The install test here checks chart changes against the pinned `appVersion`. Its job is good coverage of chart changes, so it does not need a more complex install.

The install test runs on kind, which runs the standard Kubernetes control plane without bundled extras and can pin a Kubernetes version per node image. k3s starts a little faster, but it bundles Traefik, ServiceLB and kine, and moving to it would not give us any code to share with n8n's suite.

Each install leg installs an example file with an overlay from `ci/install/`, which replaces the example's placeholders and scales it down to fit a hosted runner. An example gets a leg by having an overlay. Postgres and Redis come from plain manifests in `ci/fixtures/` on the official `postgres` and `redis` images. This follows "State is external and reached through a contract": the chart needs a hostname and an existing Secret, and nothing more. The fixtures are test scaffolding, not a recommendation for running either datastore.

## Consequences

The install test depends on no third-party chart repository. A render break in any example fails `template-validation` on the pull request that caused it. An install break in `minimal.yaml`, `standalone.yaml` or `task-runners.yaml` fails `install-test` on labelled, bump and release pull requests. The other examples are rendered but not installed until they have an overlay. Most of them need a licence, S3, KEDA, an ingress controller or labelled nodes first. The fixture image versions in `ci/fixtures/` are pinned and move by hand.

name: CI

on:
  push:
    branches: [main, "release/**"]
  # No base-branch filter, so a pull request stacked on another one gets CI
  # too.
  pull_request:
    # The first three are the defaults, respelled because naming any type
    # replaces them. `labeled` is what makes adding test-install to an open PR
    # actually run install-test, which previously did nothing until the next
    # push. `unlabeled` is its counterpart: without it, taking the label off a
    # PR whose install-test failed would leave the red ci-ok standing and block
    # a PR that never needed the test. Any label change triggers a run, not
    # just that one.
    types: [opened, synchronize, reopened, labeled, unlabeled]

permissions:
  contents: read
  security-events: write

jobs:
  # Where the install-test policy lives, in one place, so that the job's
  # condition and the ci-ok check below cannot drift apart.
  #
  # It runs automatically for the version bump PRs and for release-please's PRs,
  # both of which auto-merge or release off the back of it, and on demand for
  # anything else a maintainer labels. Only write access can add a label, and
  # the branch names are only honoured on a branch in this repository, so a
  # fork PR cannot name its way into a kind cluster.
  #
  # test-install runs the examples on the chart's appVersion. On pull requests
  # to main, test-install-v3-rc runs them again on the newest n8n 3 release
  # candidate, so the chart 2.0 work can be checked against n8n 3 before
  # appVersion moves to it.
  #
  # upgrade-test runs on demand only, on pull requests to main.
  gate:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    env:
      # The maintenance branch for the previous chart major. upgrade-test
      # installs that major's last release with this branch's examples, then
      # upgrades to the pull request.
      UPGRADE_FROM: release/n8n-2.x
    outputs:
      install-test: ${{ steps.decide.outputs.install-test }}
      install-examples: ${{ steps.examples.outputs.examples }}
      install-n8n: ${{ steps.decide.outputs.install-n8n }}
      upgrade-test: ${{ steps.decide.outputs.upgrade-test }}
      upgrade-examples: ${{ steps.examples.outputs.upgrade-examples }}
      upgrade-from: ${{ env.UPGRADE_FROM }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with:
          sparse-checkout: charts/n8n/ci/install

      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with:
          ref: ${{ env.UPGRADE_FROM }}
          path: previous
          sparse-checkout: charts/n8n/ci/install

      # An example gets an install leg by having an overlay in ci/install/,
      # and an upgrade leg by having one on both branches. Overlays that read
      # the n8n-license Secret need the licence repo secrets, which fork pull
      # requests do not receive, so those legs are left out when the secrets
      # are missing.
      - name: List the examples install-test covers
        id: examples
        env:
          HAS_LICENCE: ${{ secrets.N8N_LICENSE_ACTIVATION_KEY != '' && secrets.N8N_LICENSE_TENANT_ID != '' }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          examples=()
          upgrades=()
          for overlay in charts/n8n/ci/install/*.yaml; do
            example=$(basename "$overlay" .yaml)
            previous="previous/charts/n8n/ci/install/${example}.yaml"
            if [[ "$HAS_LICENCE" != "true" ]] && grep -qs 'name: n8n-license' "$overlay" "$previous"; then
              echo "::notice::Skipping the ${example} install and upgrade legs: the licence secrets are not available."
              continue
            fi
            examples+=("$example")
            if [[ -f "$previous" ]]; then
              upgrades+=("$example")
            fi
          done
          for previous in previous/charts/n8n/ci/install/*.yaml; do
            example=$(basename "$previous" .yaml)
            if [[ ! -f "charts/n8n/ci/install/${example}.yaml" ]]; then
              echo "::notice::No upgrade leg for ${example}: this branch has no overlay for it."
            fi
          done
          json=$(printf '%s\n' "${examples[@]}" | jq -R 'select(length > 0)' | jq -sc .)
          echo "examples=$json" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          echo "install-test examples: $json"
          json=$(printf '%s\n' "${upgrades[@]}" | jq -R 'select(length > 0)' | jq -sc .)
          echo "upgrade-examples=$json" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          echo "upgrade-test examples: $json"

      - name: Decide whether install-test runs
        id: decide
        env:
          EVENT: ${{ github.event_name }}
          LABELLED: ${{ contains(github.event.pull_request.labels.*.name, 'test-install') }}
          UPGRADE_LABELLED: ${{ contains(github.event.pull_request.labels.*.name, 'test-upgrade') }}
          UPGRADE_EXAMPLES: ${{ steps.examples.outputs.upgrade-examples }}
          V3_RC_LABELLED: ${{ contains(github.event.pull_request.labels.*.name, 'test-install-v3-rc') }}
          BASE_REF: ${{ github.event.pull_request.base.ref }}
          SAME_REPO: ${{ github.event.pull_request.head.repo.full_name == github.repository }}
          HEAD_REF: ${{ github.event.pull_request.head.ref }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail

          versions=()
          if [[ "$EVENT" == "pull_request" ]]; then
            if [[ "$LABELLED" == "true" ]]; then
              versions+=(appVersion)
            elif [[ "$SAME_REPO" == "true" ]] &&
                 [[ "$HEAD_REF" == automated/bump-n8n* || "$HEAD_REF" == release-please--* ]]; then
              versions+=(appVersion)
            fi

            # The dated tag that v3-rc points at, so the run names the build it
            # tested. Both images publish the same tags, and the runner image
            # follows image.tag.
            if [[ "$V3_RC_LABELLED" == "true" && "$BASE_REF" == "main" ]]; then
              hub=https://hub.docker.com/v2/repositories
              digest=$(curl -sSf "$hub/n8nio/n8n/tags/v3-rc" | jq -r .digest)
              tag=$(curl -sSf "$hub/n8nio/n8n/tags?page_size=100&name=v3-rc-" |
                jq -r --arg digest "$digest" '[.results[]
                  | select(.digest == $digest and (.name | test("^v3-rc-[0-9]{8}(\\.[0-9]+)?$")))
                  | .name] | sort | last // empty')
              if [[ -z "$tag" ]]; then
                echo "::error::No dated n8n tag matches v3-rc ($digest)."
                exit 1
              fi
              if ! curl -sSf -o /dev/null "$hub/n8nio/runners/tags/$tag"; then
                echo "::error::n8nio/runners has no $tag tag to match n8nio/n8n."
                exit 1
              fi
              echo "v3-rc is $tag."
              versions+=("$tag")
            fi
          fi

          run=false
          if [[ ${#versions[@]} -gt 0 ]]; then
            run=true
          fi
          json=$(printf '%s\n' "${versions[@]}" | jq -R 'select(length > 0)' | jq -sc .)
          echo "install-test=$run" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          echo "install-n8n=$json" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          echo "install-test on this event: $run, on n8n $json"

          # Only main is a major ahead of UPGRADE_FROM. A maintenance branch
          # has no newer major to upgrade to.
          upgrade=false
          if [[ "$EVENT" == "pull_request" && "$UPGRADE_LABELLED" == "true" && "$BASE_REF" == "main" && "$UPGRADE_EXAMPLES" != "[]" ]]; then
            upgrade=true
          fi

          echo "upgrade-test=$upgrade" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          echo "upgrade-test on this event: $upgrade"

  lint:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0

      - uses: azure/setup-helm@v4
        with:
          version: "3.17.0"

      - uses: actions/setup-python@v5
        with:
          python-version: "3.12"

      - uses: helm/chart-testing-action@v2.7.0

      - name: Run chart-testing (lint)
        run: ct lint --chart-dirs charts --charts charts/n8n --validate-maintainers=false

  unittest:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      # Pinned apart from the other jobs: helm-unittest 1.1 does not load on
      # Helm 3.17, and 1.0 has no --skip-schema-validation.
      - uses: azure/setup-helm@v4
        with:
          version: "3.22.0"

      - name: Install helm-unittest
        run: helm plugin install https://github.com/helm-unittest/helm-unittest.git --version v1.1.2

      - name: Run unit tests
        run: helm unittest --strict charts/n8n

      # These cases cover fail calls that values.schema.json reaches first.
      - name: Run unit tests without schema validation
        run: helm unittest --strict --skip-schema-validation -f 'tests/without-schema/*_test.yaml' charts/n8n

  # Renders every file in examples/, new ones included.
  template-validation:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - uses: azure/setup-helm@v4
        with:
          version: "3.17.0"

      - name: Render every example
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail

          failed=0
          for f in charts/n8n/examples/*.yaml; do
            echo "Rendering $f"
            if ! helm template test charts/n8n -f "$f" --dry-run=client > /dev/null; then
              echo "::error file=$f::$f does not render."
              failed=1
            fi
          done

          exit "$failed"

      - name: Validate extraContainers (minimal + ci overlay)
        run: helm template test charts/n8n -f charts/n8n/examples/minimal.yaml -f charts/n8n/ci/extraContainers-values.yaml --dry-run=client > /dev/null

  # helm template proves the chart produces YAML, not that the API server
  # accepts it. This checks every example against the Kubernetes schemas for
  # the chart's minimum version and the newest one with published schemas,
  # and the CRDs the examples use against the community catalogue. A kind
  # with no schema is an error, so a new CRD needs a schema source.
  kubeconform:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    env:
      KUBECONFORM_VERSION: v0.8.0
      KUBECONFORM_SHA256: 9bc2bffbf71f261128533edaf912153948b7ff238f9a531ae6d34466ec287883
      # The newest Kubernetes release in kubernetes-json-schema. The minimum
      # comes from kubeVersion in Chart.yaml.
      KUBERNETES_NEWEST: 1.37.1
      # Both schema sources are pinned to a commit, so results do not move
      # under a pull request.
      K8S_SCHEMAS: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/yannh/kubernetes-json-schema/8df8a883b68a24a104b4a9e43c1288090ae60b3b/{{.NormalizedKubernetesVersion}}-standalone{{.StrictSuffix}}/{{.ResourceKind}}{{.KindSuffix}}.json
      CRD_SCHEMAS: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/datreeio/CRDs-catalog/fd90051867733c60d32d16450556e9cd18459aef/{{.Group}}/{{.ResourceKind}}_{{.ResourceAPIVersion}}.json
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - uses: azure/setup-helm@v4
        with:
          version: "3.17.0"

      - name: Install kubeconform
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          curl -sSfLo kubeconform.tar.gz "https://github.com/yannh/kubeconform/releases/download/${KUBECONFORM_VERSION}/kubeconform-linux-amd64.tar.gz"
          echo "${KUBECONFORM_SHA256}  kubeconform.tar.gz" | sha256sum -c -
          tar -xzf kubeconform.tar.gz -C /usr/local/bin kubeconform
          rm kubeconform.tar.gz
          kubeconform -v

      - name: Validate every example
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail

          minimum=$(grep -E '^kubeVersion:' charts/n8n/Chart.yaml | grep -oE '[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+' | head -1 || true)
          if [[ -z "$minimum" ]]; then
            echo "::error file=charts/n8n/Chart.yaml::Could not read the minimum Kubernetes version from kubeVersion."
            exit 1
          fi

          if [[ "$(printf '%s\n' "$minimum" "$KUBERNETES_NEWEST" | sort -V | head -1)" != "$minimum" ]]; then
            echo "::error::KUBERNETES_NEWEST ($KUBERNETES_NEWEST) is older than the chart's minimum ($minimum). Raise it."
            exit 1
          fi

          # Without this, a version with no published schemas fails every
          # example with a message that hides the cause.
          for version in "$minimum" "$KUBERNETES_NEWEST"; do
            if ! probe=$(printf 'apiVersion: v1\nkind: ConfigMap\nmetadata:\n  name: probe\n' |
                 kubeconform -strict -kubernetes-version "$version" -schema-location "$K8S_SCHEMAS" - 2>&1); then
              echo "::error::Could not load the Kubernetes $version schemas from the pinned kubernetes-json-schema commit: ${probe//$'\n'/ }"
              exit 1
            fi
          done

          failed=0
          for version in "$minimum" "$KUBERNETES_NEWEST"; do
            for f in charts/n8n/examples/*.yaml; do
              echo "Validating $f against Kubernetes $version"
              if ! helm template test charts/n8n -f "$f" --kube-version "$version" |
                   kubeconform -strict -summary \
                     -kubernetes-version "$version" \
                     -schema-location "$K8S_SCHEMAS" \
                     -schema-location "$CRD_SCHEMAS" -; then
                echo "::error file=$f::$f does not validate against Kubernetes $version."
                failed=1
              fi
            done
          done

          exit "$failed"

  # Installs examples as a customer would, overriding only the placeholder
  # hosts, the Secret name and the worker count. Postgres and Redis are plain manifests on the
  # official images, so the test depends on no third-party chart repository.
  # Installs each example as a customer would, with an overlay from
  # ci/install/ that replaces its placeholders and scales it down to fit a
  # hosted runner. Postgres and Redis are plain manifests on the official
  # images. Add-ons an example expects come from their own projects' charts.
  install-test:
    name: install-test (${{ matrix.example }}${{ matrix.n8n != 'appVersion' && format(', n8n {0}', matrix.n8n) || '' }})
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    needs: gate
    if: needs.gate.outputs.install-test == 'true'
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        example: ${{ fromJSON(needs.gate.outputs.install-examples) }}
        n8n: ${{ fromJSON(needs.gate.outputs.install-n8n) }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - uses: azure/setup-helm@v4
        with:
          version: "3.17.0"

      # A leg that needs more than one node brings its own kind config.
      - name: Create kind cluster
        uses: helm/kind-action@v1.15.0
        with:
          config: ${{ hashFiles(format('charts/n8n/ci/kind/{0}.yaml', matrix.example)) != '' && format('charts/n8n/ci/kind/{0}.yaml', matrix.example) || '' }}

      # Every leg gets the same Secrets and fixtures, so an overlay only has
      # to name the hosts.
      - name: Create Secrets and start Postgres and Redis
        env:
          ACTIVATION_KEY: ${{ secrets.N8N_LICENSE_ACTIVATION_KEY }}
          TENANT_ID: ${{ secrets.N8N_LICENSE_TENANT_ID }}
        run: bash charts/n8n/ci/prepare-cluster.sh

      # <example>.pre.sh installs what the example expects the cluster to
      # provide, and <example>.post.sh checks it works with the chart.
      - name: Prepare the cluster for ${{ matrix.example }}.yaml
        if: hashFiles(format('charts/n8n/ci/install/{0}.pre.sh', matrix.example)) != ''
        env:
          EXAMPLE: ${{ matrix.example }}
        run: bash "charts/n8n/ci/install/${EXAMPLE}.pre.sh"

      - name: Install chart with ${{ matrix.example }}.yaml on n8n ${{ matrix.n8n }}
        env:
          EXAMPLE: ${{ matrix.example }}
          N8N: ${{ matrix.n8n }}
        run: |
          image=()
          if [[ "$N8N" != "appVersion" ]]; then
            image=(--set "image.tag=${N8N}")
          fi
          helm install n8n charts/n8n \
            -f "charts/n8n/examples/${EXAMPLE}.yaml" \
            -f "charts/n8n/ci/install/${EXAMPLE}.yaml" \
            "${image[@]}" \
            --wait --timeout 300s

      - name: Run helm test
        run: helm test n8n

      - name: Check ${{ matrix.example }}.yaml against the cluster
        if: hashFiles(format('charts/n8n/ci/install/{0}.post.sh', matrix.example)) != ''
        env:
          EXAMPLE: ${{ matrix.example }}
        run: bash "charts/n8n/ci/install/${EXAMPLE}.post.sh"

      - name: Show cluster state
        if: failure()
        run: |
          kubectl get pods -o wide
          kubectl get events --sort-by=.lastTimestamp | tail -30
          kubectl logs -l app.kubernetes.io/name=n8n --all-containers --tail=100 || true

  # Installs the last release of the previous chart major with that major's
  # example and overlay, then upgrades it in place to this pull request's
  # chart with this pull request's example and overlay, as a customer who has
  # migrated their values would. The cluster add-ons and hooks come from this
  # pull request, because CI stands in for the cluster the customer
  # upgrades into.
  upgrade-test:
    name: upgrade-test (${{ matrix.example }})
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    needs: gate
    if: needs.gate.outputs.upgrade-test == 'true'
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        example: ${{ fromJSON(needs.gate.outputs.upgrade-examples) }}
    env:
      EXAMPLE: ${{ matrix.example }}
      PREVIOUS: previous/charts/n8n
      CHART_REPO: oci://ghcr.io/n8n-io/n8n-helm-chart/n8n
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with:
          ref: ${{ needs.gate.outputs.upgrade-from }}
          path: previous
          sparse-checkout: |
            .release-please-manifest.json
            charts/n8n/examples
            charts/n8n/ci/install
          sparse-checkout-cone-mode: false

      - uses: azure/setup-helm@v4
        with:
          version: "3.17.0"

      - name: Create kind cluster
        uses: helm/kind-action@v1.15.0
        with:
          config: ${{ hashFiles(format('charts/n8n/ci/kind/{0}.yaml', matrix.example)) != '' && format('charts/n8n/ci/kind/{0}.yaml', matrix.example) || '' }}

      - name: Create Secrets and start Postgres and Redis
        env:
          ACTIVATION_KEY: ${{ secrets.N8N_LICENSE_ACTIVATION_KEY }}
          TENANT_ID: ${{ secrets.N8N_LICENSE_TENANT_ID }}
        run: bash charts/n8n/ci/prepare-cluster.sh

      - name: Prepare the cluster for ${{ matrix.example }}.yaml
        if: hashFiles(format('charts/n8n/ci/install/{0}.pre.sh', matrix.example)) != ''
        run: bash "charts/n8n/ci/install/${EXAMPLE}.pre.sh"

      # The maintenance branch's manifest names its major. Helm picks the
      # newest published release in it, prereleases left out.
      - name: Find the last release of the previous major
        id: previous
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          major=$(jq -r '."charts/n8n"' previous/.release-please-manifest.json | cut -d. -f1)
          version=$(helm show chart "$CHART_REPO" --version "${major}.x" | sed -n 's/^version: //p')
          echo "Upgrading from chart ${version}."
          echo "version=$version" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"

      - name: Install chart ${{ steps.previous.outputs.version }} with its ${{ matrix.example }}.yaml
        env:
          VERSION: ${{ steps.previous.outputs.version }}
        run: |
          helm install n8n "$CHART_REPO" --version "$VERSION" \
            -f "${PREVIOUS}/examples/${EXAMPLE}.yaml" \
            -f "${PREVIOUS}/ci/install/${EXAMPLE}.yaml" \
            --wait --timeout 300s

      - name: Record the release before the upgrade
        run: bash charts/n8n/ci/upgrade/resources.sh snapshot n8n "$RUNNER_TEMP/before.json"

      # A values file written for the previous major has to fail on each
      # retired key it sets, naming it. Any other reason the upgrade fails is
      # a warning, so a setting retired outside n8n.retiredKeys shows on the
      # run. --dry-run keeps the release unchanged.
      - name: Upgrade with the unmigrated values
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          files=("${PREVIOUS}/examples/${EXAMPLE}.yaml" "${PREVIOUS}/ci/install/${EXAMPLE}.yaml")
          # Captured first, because a failure inside < <(...) would read as
          # an empty list and skip the check.
          keys=$(bash charts/n8n/ci/upgrade/retired-keys.sh charts/n8n "${files[@]}")
          mapfile -t retired < <(printf '%s' "$keys" | sed '/^$/d')
          echo "The unmigrated ${EXAMPLE}.yaml sets these retired keys: ${retired[*]:-none}"

          if output=$(helm upgrade n8n charts/n8n -f "${files[0]}" -f "${files[1]}" --dry-run 2>&1); then
            if [[ ${#retired[@]} -gt 0 ]]; then
              echo "::error::helm upgrade accepted the unmigrated ${EXAMPLE}.yaml, which sets ${retired[*]}."
              exit 1
            fi
            echo "helm upgrade accepts the unmigrated ${EXAMPLE}.yaml."
            exit 0
          fi
          echo "$output"

          failed=0
          for key in "${retired[@]}"; do
            if ! grep -qF " ${key} is no longer a chart value." <<< "$output"; then
              echo "::error::helm upgrade failed on the unmigrated ${EXAMPLE}.yaml without naming ${key}."
              failed=1
            fi
          done

          # n8n.validate reports one problem as the error itself and several
          # as a list.
          if grep -q 'problems in your values:$' <<< "$output"; then
            problems=$(sed -n 's/^- //p' <<< "$output")
          else
            problems=$(sed -n 's/^Error: \(UPGRADE FAILED: \)\{0,1\}\(execution error at ([^)]*): \)\{0,1\}//p' <<< "$output")
          fi
          while IFS= read -r problem; do
            if [[ -n "$problem" && "$problem" != *" is no longer a chart value. "* ]]; then
              echo "::warning::The unmigrated ${EXAMPLE}.yaml fails outside n8n.retiredKeys: ${problem}"
            fi
          done <<< "$problems"
          exit "$failed"

      - name: Upgrade to this chart with ${{ matrix.example }}.yaml
        run: |
          helm upgrade n8n charts/n8n \
            -f "charts/n8n/examples/${EXAMPLE}.yaml" \
            -f "charts/n8n/ci/install/${EXAMPLE}.yaml" \
            --wait --timeout 300s

      - name: Check the upgrade recreated nothing and rolled once
        run: bash charts/n8n/ci/upgrade/resources.sh compare n8n "$RUNNER_TEMP/before.json"

      - name: Run helm test
        run: helm test n8n

      - name: Check ${{ matrix.example }}.yaml against the cluster
        if: hashFiles(format('charts/n8n/ci/install/{0}.post.sh', matrix.example)) != ''
        run: bash "charts/n8n/ci/install/${EXAMPLE}.post.sh"

      - name: Show cluster state
        if: failure()
        run: |
          helm history n8n || true
          kubectl get pods -o wide
          kubectl get events --sort-by=.lastTimestamp | tail -30
          kubectl logs -l app.kubernetes.io/name=n8n --all-containers --tail=100 || true

  security-scan:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - name: Run Trivy vulnerability scanner
        uses: aquasecurity/trivy-action@57a97c7e7821a5776cebc9bb87c984fa69cba8f1 # v0.35.0
        with:
          scan-type: fs
          scan-ref: charts/n8n
          format: sarif
          output: trivy-results.sarif

      - name: Upload Trivy scan results
        uses: github/codeql-action/upload-sarif@v3
        if: github.event_name != 'pull_request' || github.event.pull_request.head.repo.full_name == github.repository
        with:
          sarif_file: trivy-results.sarif

  # The single check to require on main. It exists for two reasons: a skipped
  # job reports success to required status checks, so requiring install-test
  # or upgrade-test directly would let a PR merge untested if its condition
  # ever stopped matching, and both are matrices whose leg names would
  # otherwise all need listing in the ruleset.
  ci-ok:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    if: always()
    needs: [gate, lint, unittest, template-validation, kubeconform, install-test, upgrade-test, security-scan]
    steps:
      - name: Check the other jobs
        env:
          GATE: ${{ needs.gate.result }}
          LINT: ${{ needs.lint.result }}
          UNITTEST: ${{ needs.unittest.result }}
          TEMPLATES: ${{ needs['template-validation'].result }}
          KUBECONFORM: ${{ needs.kubeconform.result }}
          SECURITY: ${{ needs['security-scan'].result }}
          INSTALL: ${{ needs['install-test'].result }}
          INSTALL_REQUIRED: ${{ needs.gate.outputs.install-test }}
          UPGRADE: ${{ needs['upgrade-test'].result }}
          UPGRADE_REQUIRED: ${{ needs.gate.outputs.upgrade-test }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail

          failed=0

          for job in "gate:$GATE" "lint:$LINT" "unittest:$UNITTEST" "template-validation:$TEMPLATES" "kubeconform:$KUBECONFORM" "security-scan:$SECURITY"; do
            if [[ "${job#*:}" != "success" ]]; then
              echo "::error::${job%%:*} did not pass, it was ${job#*:}."
              failed=1
            fi
          done

          # install-test is allowed to be skipped, but only where the gate said
          # it was not needed. Skipped on a PR that needed it is a failure.
          if [[ "$INSTALL_REQUIRED" == "true" && "$INSTALL" != "success" ]]; then
            echo "::error::install-test had to pass on this pull request, but it was $INSTALL."
            failed=1
          fi

          if [[ "$UPGRADE_REQUIRED" == "true" && "$UPGRADE" != "success" ]]; then
            echo "::error::upgrade-test had to pass on this pull request, but it was $UPGRADE."
            failed=1
          fi

          if [[ "$failed" == "1" ]]; then
            exit 1
          fi

          echo "All required jobs passed (install-test: $INSTALL, required: ${INSTALL_REQUIRED:-false}; upgrade-test: $UPGRADE, required: ${UPGRADE_REQUIRED:-false})."

# n8n on Subfolder with SSL

Starts n8n and deploys it on a subfolder

## Start

To start n8n in a subfolder simply start docker-compose by executing the following
command in the current folder.

**IMPORTANT:** But before you do that change the default users and passwords in the `.env` file!

```
docker compose up -d
```

To stop it execute:

```
docker compose stop
```

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Checks both mains are up in multi-main mode and the licence is active. The
# mains share one database, so only the first to start activates the licence.
# A main that finds the licence already stored, as every main does after an
# upgrade, logs the stored cert's state instead, which has to be valid.
set -euo pipefail

ready=$(kubectl get deploy n8n-main -o jsonpath='{.status.readyReplicas}')
if [[ "$ready" != "2" ]]; then
  echo "::error::Expected 2 ready mains, found ${ready:-0}."
  exit 1
fi

# Logs are read into a variable first: piping kubectl into grep -q can end
# the pipeline with SIGPIPE, which pipefail reports as a failure.
for _ in $(seq 1 15); do
  for pod in $(kubectl get pods -l app.kubernetes.io/component=main -o name); do
    logs=$(kubectl logs "$pod" --all-containers)
    if grep -q 'license successfully activated' <<< "$logs"; then
      echo "Both mains are ready, and ${pod} activated the licence."
      exit 0
    fi
    if grep -q '\[license SDK\] cert state: .* isValid=true ' <<< "$logs"; then
      echo "Both mains are ready, and ${pod} loaded the stored licence."
      exit 0
    fi
  done
  sleep 2
done
echo "::error::No n8n-main pod activated or loaded the licence."
exit 1

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Installs the Traefik and Prometheus Operator CRDs the example's extraObjects
# need, and the n8n-tls Secret its IngressRoute names. Only the CRDs are
# installed: the leg checks the chart's templating, not Traefik's routing.
set -euo pipefail

helm repo add traefik https://traefik.github.io/charts
helm repo add prometheus-community https://prometheus-community.github.io/helm-charts

# The Traefik CRDs are too large for a Helm release Secret, so they are
# rendered and applied server-side rather than installed as a release.
helm template traefik-crds traefik/traefik-crds --version 1.18.0 | kubectl apply --server-side -f - > /dev/null
kubectl wait crd/ingressroutes.traefik.io --for=condition=Established --timeout=60s
helm install prometheus-operator-crds prometheus-community/prometheus-operator-crds \
  --version 32.0.1 --wait --timeout 120s

tls_dir=$(mktemp -d)
trap 'rm -rf "$tls_dir"' EXIT
openssl req -x509 -newkey rsa:2048 -nodes -days 1 -subj "/CN=n8n.example.com" \
  -keyout "$tls_dir/tls.key" -out "$tls_dir/tls.crt" 2> /dev/null
kubectl create secret tls n8n-tls --cert="$tls_dir/tls.crt" --key="$tls_dir/tls.key"

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Checks each n8n pod selects, and landed in, the pool
# examples/node-placement.yaml asks for. A pod that lost its nodeSelector can
# still land in the right pool by chance, so the selector is checked as well
# as the node.
set -euo pipefail

check() {
  local component=$1 pool=$2
  local pods found=0
  pods=$(kubectl get pods -l "app.kubernetes.io/component=${component}" \
    -o jsonpath='{range .items[*]}{.metadata.name}{" "}{.spec.nodeName}{" "}{.spec.nodeSelector.pool}{"\n"}{end}')
  while read -r pod node selector; do
    [[ -z "$pod" ]] && continue
    found=1
    if [[ "$selector" != "$pool" ]]; then
      echo "::error::${pod} selects pool '${selector}', expected '${pool}'."
      exit 1
    fi
    actual=$(kubectl get node "$node" -o jsonpath='{.metadata.labels.pool}')
    if [[ "$actual" != "$pool" ]]; then
      echo "::error::${pod} is on ${node} (pool '${actual}'), expected pool '${pool}'."
      exit 1
    fi
  done <<< "$pods"
  if [[ "$found" == 0 ]]; then
    echo "::error::No ${component} pods found."
    exit 1
  fi
  echo "${component} pods are in pool ${pool}."
}

check main n8n-frontend
check webhook-processor n8n-frontend
check worker n8n-workers

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# n8n checks the S3 bucket before it reports ready, and S3 binary storage
# needs the licence, so healthy mains in S3 mode have already activated the
# licence and reached the bucket. This confirms each main configured the mock
# rather than another endpoint.
set -euo pipefail

pods=$(kubectl get pods -l app.kubernetes.io/component=main -o name)
if [[ -z "$pods" ]]; then
  echo "::error::No n8n-main pods found."
  exit 1
fi
# Logs are read into a variable first: piping kubectl into grep -q can end
# the pipeline with SIGPIPE, which pipefail reports as a failure.
for pod in $pods; do
  logs=$(kubectl logs "$pod" --all-containers)
  if ! grep -q 'S3 binary storage configured: endpoint=http://s3mock:9090' <<< "$logs"; then
    echo "::error::${pod} did not configure S3 binary storage against the mock."
    exit 1
  fi
done
echo "Every main stores binary data in the S3 mock."
